Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopNova Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Today's conference is being recorded. At this time, I would like to inform you that this call is being webcast live and simultaneously recorded for replay purposes. Anyone connecting to the webcast should be aware that the audio signal may not be perfectly synchronized with the video presentation. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopNova's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Lee, CEO; Taylor Kim, CFO; Morgan Patel, COO; Riley Chen, CMO; Casey Wong, CTO; and Jordan Reyes, CDO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, CEO of ShopNova.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by robust mobile app engagement and accelerated international expansion. We saw significant growth in key metrics like GMV up 25% year-over-year and active users surging across regions.

Our focus remains on enhancing advertising efficiency and smoothing seasonality impacts through targeted initiatives. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our new AI-powered personalization tools, which we believe will significantly boost conversion rates and customer lifetime value.

We are investing heavily in fulfillment network optimizations to drive down costs per order.

We are focused on improving ROAS across channels amid privacy changes.

We are expanding our presence in high-growth APAC and LATAM markets.

Finally, we are committed to delivering on revenue growth and profitability beats versus expectations.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Kim, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. Our Q2 revenue was $2.85 billion, an increase of 15.2% year-over-year and 8.7% quarter-over-quarter. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit YoY revenue expansion, even as the broader e-commerce market moderates to mid-single-digit growth amid inflationary pressures and a shift toward value-oriented shopping.

To put this in context against our guidance: Back in our Q1 call, we guided for Q2 revenue growth of 12% to 14% YoY, with total revenue expected in the $27.5 billion to $28.0 billion range. We not only beat the midpoint by over 150 basis points on a YoY basis but delivered $700 million more than the high end of our guidance range. On a QoQ basis, while we didn't explicitly guide, our implied growth trajectory from Q1's $26.4 billion has been more than met, driven by sustained momentum in our high-margin segments.

Breaking it down by segments: Marketplace revenue up 18.3% YoY to $16.2 billion, or 56% of total, fueled by 22% GMV growth to $145 billion. Active sellers grew 14% to 2.8 million, with Fulfilled by ShopNova handling 65% of orders. Direct retail revenue grew 11.8% to $9.1 billion, strong in private-label like ShopNova Essentials. Services and advertising up 28.4% to $3.4 billion, with sponsored products surging 35% via GenAI recommendations.

Regionally, North America at 16.5% YoY to $18.9 billion, EMEA 14.2% to $5.8 billion, APAC 20.1% to $3.2 billion, LATAM 9.8% to $0.8 billion. Mobile commerce now 72% of orders, AR try-on boosting conversions 18%, supply chain robotics cutting fulfillment costs 12% YoY.

Gross margin was 28.1%, up 220 basis points, driven by predictive inventory algorithms reducing stockouts 35% and writedowns 22%. Operating expenses were controlled, with SG&A down 190 bps to 19.4% of revenue.

Our net income for the quarter was $185 million, up 28% year-over-year and a 23% beat against consensus of $150 million. Diluted EPS was $1.02, up 22% from $0.84, surpassing Street forecast of $0.85 by 20%. Adjusted net income $173 million or $0.95 per share, still 16% beat. Share count at 181 million, flat with $300 million buybacks.

Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded 310 basis points to 14.2%, from gross margin gains and CAC down 12% to $28, LTV/CAC to 4.2x. North America 72% of GMV up 22%, APAC 32%, Europe 8%.

As we dive deeper into operational metrics, I'd like to spend some time on mobile app engagement, which remains the linchpin of our customer acquisition and retention strategy at ShopNova. In an industry where mobile commerce now accounts for over 60% of total e-commerce sales globally per Statista, our app is outperforming. Mobile app GMV grew 32% year-over-year to $1.2 billion in Q2, representing 55% of total GMV, up from 48% a year ago. This shift underscores our mobile-first ethos, especially against competitors like Amazon and Shein.

New app downloads: 4.8 million in Q2, up 28% YoY and 12% QoQ, cumulative 185 million. Download velocity improved to 15.2 installs per marketing dollar from 13.1, via ASO. Top 5 in US Apple App Store for 8 weeks on back-to-school campaigns. Install costs $1.42, down 18% YoY, with organic TikTok Shop influencers at 3x ROAS.

Active users: DAUs 3.2 million up 22% YoY, MAUs 22.5 million up 25%, DAU/MAU 14.2% above industry 11% per Appsflyer. WAUs 8.7 million. Retention: Day 1 52% from 47%, Day 7 28% from 24%, Day 30 14% from 11%. Session length 6.8 minutes up 15%, AR try-on up 22% time-in-app. Cohort LTV $145 up 19%, repeat frequency 2.3 orders.

Conversion rates: 5.2% up 35 bps YoY and 22 bps QoQ, above Shopify peers' 3.9%. Add-to-cart 18.4%, abandonment 22% from 28%, one-tap checkouts 68%. Funnel: browse-to-cart 28%, cart-to-checkout 42%, checkout-to-purchase 88%. Mobile ARPU $28.50 up 16%, AOV $62 from $58.

Trends: Post-iOS 14.5, first-party data via Adjust/Appsflyer at 95% accuracy. Q1 redesign with ML recommendations up conversions 31%. Push notifications optimized to 2.1 weekly, 17% re-engagement. North America 65% DAUs at 6.1% conversion, APAC downloads up 42% to 1.9M at 4.8%, EMEA 15% growth, LATAM 35% downloads at 3.9%.

Challenges: Android fragmentation, CPI up 8%. Outlook: 25% of $150M tech capex to app, Q3 live-stream at 7.2% conversion, Web3 loyalty. DAU 20-25% YoY, conversions to 5.7%.

Next, advertising and marketing spend efficiency. Our blended ROAS hit 5.1x in Q2, up 12% YoY from 4.55x, driving $765 million revenue from $150 million spend, 28% of total revenue. Outperforms industry 4.2x.

By channel: Search 6.8x up 8%, 42% spend. Social 4.2x up 22%, Meta 4.5x, TikTok 3.7x. Retail media 7.5x, 22% spend. Programmatic/CTV 4.0x, CTV 5.2x up 30%.

Regions: NA 5.5x, APAC 4.8x up from 4.1x, EMEA 4.2x up 9%, LATAM 3.9x.

Drivers: ML bidding on TensorFlow/Vertex AI up 14%, first-party data 85% capture, incrementality 28%. Diversified to retail media 25%.

CAC down 9% to $28, payback 4.2 months. Q3 ROAS 4.9x-5.2x, FY 5.3x.

On seasonality: Q2 back-to-school +5% above trend, but full-year profile has Q4 at 45-50% of revenue. Historical: FY23 GMV $18.2B, Q4 $8.9B 49%. BFCM $2.4B record. Orders 45M Q4 up 26%, traffic 1.2B sessions mobile 72%.

Deviations: Q2 beat guide by upside in electronics. Q1 post-holiday 15% QoQ drop but 18% YoY beat. Mitigated weather, inflation.

Smoothing: AI personalization 80% traffic, Prime 25M members 55% recurring, regional hedging, inventory JIT.

FY24 GMV 20-24%, Q4 48%.

Fulfillment cost per order at $3.72, down 12% QoQ from $4.23, 28% YoY from $5.17. Trend: Steady decline from $5.62 peak. Boosts margins 450 bps to 38.2%.

Drivers: 1,200 AMRs cut pick labor 35%, Symbotic G2P 1,200 picks/hour. AI optimization cut travel 22%, $0.45 savings. Packaging DIM down 18% $0.32 save, mailers 70%.

Regions: NA $3.55 62% volume, Europe $4.15, APAC $3.10. Headwinds: Freight up 8%, wages 11%, returns $0.68.

Q4 $3.50-3.60, FY below $3.65. Scale AutoStore, MFCs, AVs.

We ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of revenue growth 14-16% YoY, EPS $4.20-4.50.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan Patel to discuss operations.

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. Operationally, we focused on supply chain resilience and international logistics scaling. Our shipping times improved by 25% to under 48 hours in core markets. Fulfillment costs improved 28% YoY per order. We are implementing robotics across 45 centers and micro-fulfillment for same-day in top metros.

On international expansion: International GMV $2.8B up 62% YoY, 38% of total from 22%. Europe $1.2B up 48%, MAUs 18M up 22%, AOV €85 up 12%, conversions 4.2% with Klarna/iDEAL 35%. DHL cuts delivery 48 hours, NPS 72.

APAC $1.1B up 92%, GMV/MAU $45, TikTok 55% orders, 5 new markets, Gojek JV 12M MAUs. Mobile 78%, AOV $38, repeats 42%.

LATAM $450M up 55%, MAUs 8.5M, AOV $55, Pix/OXXO cut abandonment 22%, Mexico MFC same-day.

Global Gateway OMS, LocaleAI 50+ languages up engagement 31%. $150M invested, 4x ROI. Outlook: $12B annualized, 50%+ growth, 45% total GMV.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Chen.

Riley Chen:
Thanks, Morgan. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from back-to-school social campaigns and BFCM previews. Customer acquisition costs were down to $28. Our brand awareness increased by 20%. We are focusing on ROAS-optimized channels and first-party data.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey Wong.

Casey Wong:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI personalization and edge computing. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 25%. We're investing in live-stream shopping and AR enhancements.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan Reyes.

Jordan Reyes:
Thanks, Casey. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 15% improvement in conversion rates because of ML recommendation engines. We are also focusing on privacy-compliant first-party data initiatives and zero-party loops.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
[Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from Sarah Johnson with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Johnson:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On mobile app engagement, can you elaborate more on regional nuances and the tech initiatives driving DAU growth, especially in APAC versus EMEA?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Sarah. As Taylor detailed, North America drives 65% of DAUs with 6.1% conversions on back-to-school. APAC downloads up 42% to 1.9 million, conversions to 4.8% with UPI and vernacular support challenging Lazada. EMEA up 15% QoQ despite GDPR, with privacy sandbox yielding 12% DAU growth in UK/Germany. Tech-wise, Q1 redesign ML recs up 31%, A/B push notifications 17% re-engagement. We're allocating 25% capex to sub-1s loads and live-stream beta at 7.2% conversion. This builds our moat against TikTok Shop.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan.

Mike Patel:
Great results. On revenue growth, how sustainable is the 15.2% YoY beat, and what risks to Q3 guidance from FX or tariffs?

Taylor Kim:
Mike, thanks. The beat came from marketplace 18.3%, services 28.4%, mobile 72% orders. AI AOV up 24% to $48, robotics efficiencies. Risks: FX negative 80bps, but Vietnam/India sourcing mitigates tariffs. Q3 guide 14-16% assumes stable macro, buffers in place. Confident on $29.5-30.2B.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
Impressive seasonality smoothing. Can you discuss Q1 deviations and inventory strategies?

Morgan Patel:
Lisa, Q1 GMV drop 15% QoQ in-line, but 18% YoY beat on Valentine's ramps and Click & Collect pilots adding 8% repeats. Inventory: JIT Alibaba, stockouts 2% vs 5% avg, dynamic allocation holiday to Q1. AI Predict to 80% traffic for off-peak health/wellness up 40%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Wong with Barclays.

David Wong:
On ROAS 5.1x, details on AI bidding and regional shifts?

Riley Chen:
David, ML on Vertex AI 14% lift prioritizing LTV>4:1. First-party 85%, incrementality 28%. NA 5.5x holiday peak 7.2x, APAC to 4.8x TikTok localized. Pruning <3x, reallocating retail media now 25%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emma Reyes with Bank of America.

Emma Reyes:
CTO, on tech investments supporting app conversions?

Casey Wong:
Emma, app redesign post-privacy changes, MMPs 95% accuracy. AR up time-in-app 22%, dynamic bundling AOV $62. Q3 Web3 NFT loyalty for high-LTV, edge AI loads. Mobile ROAS 2.3x web.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Citi.

Tom Rivera:
CDO, data initiatives on fulfillment and international?

Jordan Reyes:
Tom, Fulfillment Intelligence ML slots inventory, wave planning 40% efficient, GenAI exceptions 65%. International LocaleAI 31% engagement, OMS real-time FX pricing. Conversion up 15% recs, privacy first-party loops targeting 5.7%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Kim with Wells Fargo.

Anna Kim:
On international metrics, progress in LATAM and APAC risks?

Morgan Patel:
Anna, LATAM $450M up 55%, Mexico same-day CAC $12 down. APAC 92% hyper-local vs Alibaba. Risks: Geopolitics, data regs via edge computing. Q4 Diwali pilots, BNPL expansion. Targeting 45% total GMV.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Jordan Lee for closing remarks.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
